subject: Time-stratified analysis of geologically complex regions

messages.author: 4f106c8e6f09dbec
messages.subject: Time-stratified analysis of geologically complex regions
parts:
Hi Nick,

I have stumbled across a tricky problem in the Malay archipelago when trying to set up time-stratified models: some regions, e.g. the Philippines, Sulawesi, or the Moluccas, were independent islands for most of the geological past and reached their current composition only within the last 5 million years or so. To complicate matters more, some of these independent islands moved around a lot in the past - such as Halmahera, which super rapidly moved from north of New Guinea to the north of the Moluccas.

Currently, I have rather arbitrarily assigned just one of the "fragments" of my biogeographic regions that I track through time to estimate distances etc. for a time-stratified model. But that is not super satisfying because it oversimplifies things. Can you think of any way to keep track of the possibility that a species was on either the different fragments that make up these regions today, e.g. by coding species occurring on the Philippines as occupying two areas that had different pasts? Or do you think that would be a waste of time?

Cheers,
Ben
